speakers.name: Cindy Olsen
speakers.title: Head of Investor Relations and Strategy

exchanges.question: Can management quantify the encouraging quarter-to-date April trends; and what specific elements of Fernando Machado's QSR experience will he bring to Chipotle?
exchanges.answer: April saw a nice step up, partly from Easter being about two weeks earlier, but more from Cilantro Lime Sauce, which is outperforming Red Chimichurri with about 2x incidence, plus the rewards relaunch; no specific number given. Boatwright: after a comprehensive search, Machado was chosen for his global brand-building record and his love for the brand and fresh food, and his view of where to take advertising next was 'groundbreaking'.

exchanges.question: What was the monthly comp cadence through the quarter and what Q2 comp does the guide embed; and how fast is loyalty membership growing and is the revamp aimed at new, lapsed or existing members?
exchanges.answer: January protein campaign drove a double-digit % increase in double protein and single tacos, sustained through April, while weather closed about half of restaurants at one point, costing about 100 basis points to the quarter; February improved with Chicken al Pastor (highest incidence of its three runs); March softened around the start of the Iran conflict; April stepped up. Q2 comps are anticipated around +1%, including a modest Honey Chicken lift, which underpins expense guidance. Boatwright: since the relaunch new members are up about 25%, widening the funnel and reactivating lapsed users while deepening engagement via chips and guac welcome offer, monthly drops and Rewards on Repeat.

exchanges.question: Is the base case that sticky LTO lifts plus easier comparisons make comps accelerate through the year absent environmental deterioration; and will brand-new LTOs matter more than repeat favorites going forward?
exchanges.answer: 'That's exactly right': the demand map refresh showed consumers wanted more frequent innovation, so LTO cadence and stage-gating have doubled, alongside the app relaunch and culturally relevant marketing, with Fernando joining in the next couple of weeks. New center-of-the-plate protein LTOs are in process or test now, with more tests late in the year to inform the 2027 strategy, mixing occasional favorites with new items.

exchanges.question: What were the traffic, check and mix components of the comp and the mix outlook; and what specifically is changing on hospitality after the managers conference?
exchanges.answer: On a +0.5% comp, transactions rose about 60 basis points and check fell about 10 basis points, with price about 90 basis points and mix a drag of about 100 basis points from lower group size (post-COVID normalization, free-entree redemptions, some BYOC cannibalization, protein cups/single tacos), partly offset by extra meat and sauces; mix expected closer to flat in Q2, H2 depends on LTOs and sauces. Boatwright: guests became more discerning about hospitality, so AMC pushed treating guests like guests in your home; results include better staffing KPIs, GM turnover at historical lows and rising taste-of-food and GSAT scores.

exchanges.question: Given a possible pricing perception issue, how much will Fernando Machado integrate value and price points into the marketing message?
exchanges.answer: Chipotle is open to testing ideas without handicapping Machado, while not detracting from brand health; Boatwright believes the price point is very fair. Having underpriced the industry for the second consecutive year, Chipotle is at a 20%-30% discount to fast casual peers, giving pricing power to use when timing is right, such as entry price points like the $3.50 high-protein taco. A test in a couple of weeks in one market will offer a Happier Hour from two to five with $2.50 tacos to study elasticity.

exchanges.question: Are transaction gaps converging for previously pressured younger and lower/middle income cohorts; and where do Europe unit economics (AUVs, margins) stand and is unit growth at an inflection?
exchanges.answer: Targeted messaging and culturally relevant moments engaged younger consumers more than over the last year, with an uptick across all ages and income cohorts in Q1; no quantified gap given. Europe is at an inflection: margins are in the double-digit range and new restaurants deliver 40% ROI in year two, so Chipotle will look for real estate more meaningfully in Central London and Germany and go as quickly as it can.

exchanges.question: With chicken, Mexican and bowl competitors growing, could Chipotle market locally against competition; and were Q1 new unit volumes light, and why?
exchanges.answer: A deep dive in New York and Florida found some cannibalization in the first six months when competitors open nearby, recovering by months six to eight, with competitors bringing more consumers to the trade area; impact is low today and national marketing has the best return on ad spend, so local bifurcation is unlikely. Rymer: new restaurant productivity is about 80%, consistent with recent years; the apparent shortfall likely reflects openings weighted later in the quarter.

exchanges.question: Is reducing the delivery price premium an opportunity to improve lower value scores in that channel; and where do store labor levels need to settle, is there more to invest?
exchanges.answer: Tests of delivery premiums on DoorDash (premium) and Uber (discount) showed they need different marketing; even with elevated marketplace pricing Chipotle is below peers, delivery is in the teens with another tick up, and order ahead surpassed 20%; Arlie Sisson, starting next week, will review aggregators to inform H2 strategy. There is more opportunity to invest in labor: HEAP adds a couple of hours of productivity reinvested in stores, plus Chipotle Kitchen and AI tools, and a plan to ensure manager coverage at all 14 lunch and dinner peaks, where Chipotle is challenged today.

exchanges.question: How will restaurant margins shape up in H2 as price-inflation gap narrows, and what comp is needed for expansion; and is the HEAP comp gap widening and what is the rollout pace to 2,000?
exchanges.answer: First-half margins face the most pressure with Q1 price of 0.9% versus inflation in the mid 3% range; in H2 inflation drops as beef laps and pricing ticks up, so the dislocation should be minimal toward year-end, after which margins rise via price offsetting inflation plus transactions; no specific comp threshold given. Boatwright: HEAP restaurants show 200-400 basis points of comp lift plus throughput, taste and OSAT gains; at 600 restaurants now, installs move from 30-35 per week to 45 per week in the next month or so, reaching 2,000 by year-end and the full portfolio late 2027 or early 2028.

exchanges.question: How long after HEAP deployment does the comp improvement appear; and with marketing up about 22% in Q1 after a heavy Q4 and modest comp lift, how is incremental return measured and does it justify the spend?
exchanges.answer: About two months: a month to get proficient and a month to hit stride, then material uplift. Rymer: incremental spend supporting four LTOs and Chipotle days like the tattoo BOGO is earning good returns, each measured individually, though consumer noise remains. Boatwright: part of marketing builds brand over time, and spend continues as long as return on ad spend is responsible and margin accretive.

exchanges.question: Why does the Q2 +1% comp guide imply a roughly 50 basis point traffic decline versus Q1's gain, unless it is conservative; and what drove the 2025 rise in hourly turnover and what improves throughput beyond HEAP?
exchanges.answer: Correct: the guide is modest on lift from Chipotle Honey Chicken and other initiatives given the consumer environment, the Iran conflict and gas prices, with upside believed. Boatwright: 2025 turnover was an anomaly as sales decelerated and hours fell, plus hard decisions on hospitality fit; Q1 is back to historical low turnover levels. The throughput part of the question was not addressed.
